# Walk Stronger: how it works {: .nobreak}

<div class="chang" markdown="1">
<div class="who">Chang Yin</div>

I'm Chang. AI character. Twelve weeks, one program, done properly. Walk farther, a little faster and more confidently: walking technique, leg strength, stairs and gradual step goals.

A little more, slowly. That's the whole method.
</div>


**Who it's for.** Adults 60+ who walk (with or without a cane) and want to walk more. Walker users start at Rebuild with hallway lengths.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Ask your doctor first if:</span> Chest pain, pressure or unusual breathlessness when you walk; calf pain that comes on with walking and eases with rest; dizziness; or a recent fall: see your doctor first.
</div>


**What you need.** Walking shoes, a safe route (hallway, mall, sidewalk), stairs with a rail, a step counter or phone, a tape measure and timer for checkpoints.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Every day:</span> Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain. Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now. Pain rule (E41): Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
</div>




## Your week

Mon: strength · Tue: program session A · Wed: balance · Thu: program session B · Fri: breath + qigong · Sat: walk-and-talk · Sun: rest + stretch. Program sessions are marked in **bold** in the plan; the other days use your Strong Years Daily Practice sessions (DP numbers).

**Daily steps goal each week** (count your baseline in week 1; E22): wk 1: Baseline week: just count · wk 2: Baseline + 500/day · wk 3: Baseline + 500 · wk 4: Baseline + 500 (easy week) · wk 5: Baseline + 1,000 · wk 6: Baseline + 1,000 · wk 7: Baseline + 1,500 · wk 8: Baseline + 1,000 (easy week) · wk 9: Baseline + 2,000, up to 6,000–8,000 · wk 10: Baseline + 2,000 · wk 11: Baseline + 2,500 · wk 12: Keep 6,000–8,000 if you're there

## How it progresses

Three 4-week phases: **Foundation** (weeks 1–4, A1/B1), **Build** (weeks 5–8, A2/B2) and **Strengthen** (weeks 9–12, A3/B3).

| Week in each phase | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1st | Doses as written in the session. Learn the moves. Stop each set with one or two good reps left in the tank. |
| 2nd | Add 1–2 reps per set (never past 12). Holds up 5 seconds (never past 30). |
| 3rd | Where every rep felt easy two sessions in a row, use the Harder version or a heavier jug. Otherwise repeat week 2. |
| 4th (easy week) | Easy week: same moves, one set fewer. Then do your checkpoint at the weekend. |

**Levels.** Every session has four versions: Rebuild (chair-based), Steady, Strong and Iron. Move up only when every rep felt easy two sessions in a row. Move down any day. **Advanced** doses are never a starting point.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Red flags:</span> Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
</div>




# Your checkpoints

Start, then the end of weeks 4, 8 and 12. Same chair, same shoes, same time of day. These are fitness checks from published research, **not medical tests**.

<table class="write small"><thead><tr><th>Checkpoint</th><th>How</th><th>Start</th><th>Week 4</th><th>Week 8</th><th>Week 12</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Walking speed</strong> (E10)</td><td>Time to walk 13 feet (4 m) at your usual pace, with a 3-foot run-up. Speed (m/s) = 4 ÷ seconds. About 5 s = 0.8 m/s; 4 s = 1.0 m/s</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Timed Up and Go</strong> (E51)</td><td>Seconds, normal pace, helper beside you. 12 s or more = tell your doctor</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Two-minute step test</strong> (E49)</td><td>Right-knee lifts to the tape mark in 2 minutes, holding the counter</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Average daily steps</strong> (E22)</td><td>Average of the last 7 days</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table>

### 0:35–1:15 · Ankle pumps and circles

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps and circles</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:15 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:15–3:15 · Toe and heel walks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Toe and heel walks</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise onto the balls of your feet.</td><td>Easier: Heel raises in place</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Small steps. **Easier:** Heel raises in place instead. **Harder:** Hand hovering, still right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:15–4:35 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step up with your right foot, placing the whole foot on the step.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step, not just the toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push through the heel of the top foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:35–5:45 · Sit-to-stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Sit-to-stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Cross your arms over your chest, or rest your hands on your thighs.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Breathe in as you sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

**Cues:** Heel, roll, push. Tall. Eyes ahead. **Easier:** Normal-length steps, hand on the counter. **Harder:** 20 steps, a little faster.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:45–9:15 · Walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Easier: Indoors, touching the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk at an easy pace for 2 minutes to warm up.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Arms swing naturally.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe easy and steady. The talk test: you should be able to speak in short sentences.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:15–10:00 · Standing hip-front stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Standing hip-front stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuck your tailbone under slightly and squeeze the buttock of the back leg.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stay tall. Don't arch your back.</td><td></td></tr>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Don't arch your back. Small movement, big squeeze. **Easier:** Smaller step. **Harder:** Reach the arm on the back-leg side up toward the ceiling, to comfortable height.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:00–10:40 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

</div>

# WLK-A2 · Phase 2 (Build): Stairs and power

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walk Stronger program | 10:40 | SET-STOOP | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Phase two. Stairs and power.</td><td>Walk Stronger · A2</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail hand never lets go.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoes on.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:10 · Ankle pumps and circles

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps and circles</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:10–1:50 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. March.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:50–3:40 · Stair practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Stair practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk up one step at a time at a steady pace, whole foot on each step.</td><td>Easier: Bottom 3 steps only</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail hand never lets go.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Rest at the top as long as you like.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step. Rail hand never lets go. **Easier:** Just the bottom 3 steps, up and down. **Harder:** Two flights, or carry a light bag in the free hand.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on stairs: stop, sit, and call your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:40–5:10 · Power stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, feet flat, arms crossed or hands on thighs.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fast up, slow down.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:10–6:05 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:05–7:05 · Big-step drill

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Big-step drill</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk 10 steps a little longer than your normal step.</td><td>Easier: Normal steps, hand on counter</td></tr>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Phase three. Walk anywhere: stairs, curbs, uneven ground.</td><td>Walk Stronger · A3</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step practice, then a longer walk.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail and counter for the drills.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:10 · Ankle pumps and circles

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps and circles</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:10–2:10 · Step over a towel

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Step over a towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step over the towel sideways with the near foot, then the other.</td><td>Easier: Flat towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift the knee. Clear the towel.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Lift the knee. Clear the towel. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** A flat towel instead of rolled. **Harder:** Step over forward and back, still holding the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:10–3:30 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step up with your right foot, placing the whole foot on the step.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step, not just the toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push through the heel of the top foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:30–5:00 · Stair practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Stair practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk up one step at a time at a steady pace, whole foot on each step.</td><td>Easier: Bottom 3 steps only</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail hand never lets go.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Rest at the top as long as you like.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step. Rail hand never lets go. **Easier:** Just the bottom 3 steps, up and down. **Harder:** Two flights, or carry a light bag in the free hand.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on stairs: stop, sit, and call your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:00–9:00 · Walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Walk</td></tr>

# WLK-B3 · Phase 3 (Strengthen): The long brisk walk

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walk Stronger program | 11:10 | SET-PROM | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

# Where the numbers come from

Every number and health statement in this book traces to one of the entries below. They are the same evidence IDs our whole team uses (EVIDENCE.md). Grade A means a Cochrane review, a large meta-analysis or a guideline body. B means a single good trial or a small meta-analysis. C means an observational study: it shows a link, not cause and effect. D means lab, physiology or label data.


<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E10** (grade C). Gait speed and survival: 34,485 adults 65+. 0.8 m/s is around median life expectancy. ≥1.0 m/s was linked with longer-than-expected survival. Under 0.6 m/s means higher risk.

<p class="src">Source: Studenski et al., JAMA 2011 — https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2011/01/110104161621.htm</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E13** (grade A−). Otago Exercise Programme: a home programme of leg strengthening, balance exercises and walking designed for older adults, studied in 7 trials with 1,503 people (mean age 81.6). We use its exercise types and progressions; we make no outcome claim from it.

<p class="src">Source: Thomas et al., Age Ageing 2010 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK78898/</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E22** (grade C). Daily steps: in adults 60+, mortality benefit plateaued at about 6,000–8,000 steps/day. The top quartiles had 40–53% lower risk than the lowest (about 3,500/day).

<p class="src">Source: Paluch et al., Lancet Public Health 2022 — https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2022/03/220303112207.htm</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E23** (grade A− (meta)). Light walking after meals (even 2–5 minutes) lowers the post-meal glucose rise compared with sitting.

<p class="src">Source: Buffey et al., Sports Med 2022 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35147898/</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E41** (grade B (known literature)). Pain-monitoring model: during and after exercise, pain up to about 3/10 (we use a conservative threshold) is acceptable if it settles by the next morning and isn't trending up week to week.

<p class="src">Source: Thomeé, Phys Ther 1997; Silbernagel et al., Am J Sports Med 2007</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E42** (grade A (statement)). AHA scientific statement (2023): resistance training is recommended for adults with and without cardiovascular disease. It lowers blood pressure and improves glucose control and function. Avoid breath-holding (Valsalva). People with CVD should get individualized clearance.

<p class="src">Source: Paluch et al., Circulation 2024 — https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001189</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E43** (grade A (guideline)). Pre-exercise screening (ACSM 2015): anyone with symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease (chest pain, unusual breathlessness, fainting) should get medical clearance before starting. Otherwise, light-to-moderate exercise can begin and progress.

<p class="src">Source: Riebe et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015 (known literature)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E49** (grade A (tool/norms)). Senior Fitness Test (Rikli & Jones): 7,183 US community-dwelling adults aged 60–94 from 267 sites in 21 states. "Normal range" = the middle 50% (25th–75th percentile) for each 5-year age band and sex. 30-s chair stand, 30-s arm curl (5 lb women / 8 lb men), 2-minute step test (right-knee lifts to midway between kneecap and hip bone), chair sit-and-reach (inches, + past the toes / − short of them). Example normal ranges, women 70–74: chair stand 10–15, arm curl 12–17, step test 68–101, sit-and-reach −1.0 to +4.0 in; men 70–74: 12–17, 14–21, 80–110, −3.5 to +2.5 in. Full tables in products/strength_reset.md. It's a fitness comparison, not a diagnosis.

<p class="src">Source: Rikli & Jones, Senior Fitness Test Manual, 2nd ed. 2013 (primary not opened). Opened: normative tables — https://integrativephysicaltherapyservices.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Fitness-Testing-for-Seniors-PDF.pdf ; protocol + sample size — https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/chair-sit-and-reach/ , https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/step-test/ , https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/arm-curl/ . Note: the PDF's women 60–64 sit-and-reach cell reads "−0.5 to +0.5" (typo); we use the fitnessnorms 25th–75th percentiles (−0.6 to +4.8 in).</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E51** (grade A (tool)). CDC STEADI Timed Up and Go: stand from a chair, walk 10 feet (3 m) at normal pace, turn, walk back, sit. The CDC uses 12 seconds or more as a screening threshold worth discussing with a clinician. Always have someone stand by.

<p class="src">Source: CDC STEADI — opened https://www.cdc.gov/steadi/media/pdfs/STEADI-Assessment-TUG-508.pdf</p>

</div>
